events.title: Sulpicius Galba and Aurelius Cotta become consuls in Rome
events.description: Publius Sulpicius Galba and Gaius Aurelius Cotta took office as consuls in Rome. Sulpicius, charged with Macedonia, persuaded the Comitia centuriata at a second session to vote for war on Philip V, beginning the Second Macedonian War.

events.title: Julius Caesar assassinated on the Ides of March
events.description: A group of senators led by Brutus and Cassius stabbed Caesar to death in the Curia of Pompey. Meant to save the Republic, the murder led to civil war and the rule of Augustus.
events.html: A group of senators led by Brutus and Cassius stabbed Caesar to death in the Curia of Pompey. Meant to save the Republic, the murder led to civil war and the rule of Augustus.

events.title: Constantius II raises his cousin Gallus to the rank of caesar
events.description: As he prepared to move against the usurper Magnentius, Constantius II needed a representative in the East and made Gallus caesar at Sirmium, giving him the name Constantius and his sister Constantina in marriage. Gallus set up residence in Antioch.

events.title: Theoderic the Great kills Odoacer at Ravenna
events.description: After a long siege ended in a power-sharing agreement, Theoderic murdered Odoacer at a banquet. The Ostrogothic king then ruled Italy for over thirty years.
events.html: After a long siege ended in a power-sharing agreement, Theoderic murdered Odoacer at a banquet. The Ostrogothic king then ruled Italy for over thirty years.

events.title: Al-Hadi ila'l-Haqq Yahya arrives in Sa'dah and founds a Zaydi imamate
events.description: Invited by tribal leaders to end the strife in northern Yemen, Yahya arrived in Sa'dah and soon proclaimed himself commander of the faithful as al-Hadi. The Zaydi imams of Yemen held power in parts of the country from then until 1970.

events.title: Henry the Fowler defeats the Magyars at Riade
events.description: King Henry the Fowler of East Francia routed a Magyar army near the river Unstrut in northern Thuringia, after refusing to pay further tribute. The victory raised the prestige of the Saxon dynasty, though Magyar raids continued until 955.

events.title: Columbus returns to Spain from his first voyage
events.description: Columbus sailed into Palos, the port from which he had departed seven months earlier, with news of islands across the Atlantic. His voyages began lasting European contact with the Americas.
events.html: Columbus sailed into Palos, the port from which he had departed seven months earlier, with news of islands across the Atlantic. His voyages began lasting European contact with the Americas.

events.title: Akbar abolishes the jizya tax on non-Muslims
events.description: The Mughal emperor ended the poll tax on non-Muslim subjects, part of a policy of conciliating the Hindu majority of his empire. Aurangzeb reimposed it in 1679.
events.html: The Mughal emperor ended the poll tax on non-Muslim subjects, part of a policy of conciliating the Hindu majority of his empire. Aurangzeb reimposed it in 1679.

events.title: Maine becomes the 23rd US state
events.description: Separated from Massachusetts, Maine entered the Union as a free state under the Missouri Compromise. Its admission balanced that of Missouri as a slave state.

events.title: Tsar Nicholas II abdicates
events.description: Facing revolution in Petrograd and mutiny in the army, Nicholas II gave up the throne for himself and his son. Over three centuries of Romanov rule ended, and a Provisional Government took power.
events.html: Facing revolution in Petrograd and mutiny in the army, Nicholas II gave up the throne for himself and his son. Over three centuries of Romanov rule ended, and a Provisional Government took power.

events.title: Gunman kills 51 at two Christchurch mosques
events.description: A white supremacist attacked worshippers at Friday prayers and livestreamed the killings. Within a month New Zealand's parliament banned most semi-automatic weapons.

song: African Americans; Choctaw Freedmen of the Indian Territory
A spiritual from the 1860s about a chariot coming to carry a person home to heaven, now also sung by England rugby fans.
